title: First Representative Council of Greater Lebanon seated
why: France set up the Representative Council in 1922; first speaker took office 25 May 1922. Election date not confirmed.

title: Second Representative Council seated
why: The second Representative Council's speaker took office 13 July 1925, after the 1925 vote. Exact polling dates not confirmed.

title: General election expands Parliament to 46 members
why: 16 elected members added to 30 from the previous Representative Council; seats allotted by sect and province. Polling dates not stated.

title: Chamber elected for 1929-1932 term
why: Parliamentary term list shows a Chamber for 1929-1932; election date not found. Debbas re-elected president by it on 23 March 1929.

title: Chamber elected for 1934-1937 term
why: Term list shows a new Chamber for 1932-1937. Constitution was suspended on 9 May 1932. Polling date not found. (corrected from 1932-1937: Keghart lists the third parliament as 1934-1937.)

title: Chamber elected for 1937-1939 term
why: Term list shows a Chamber for 1937-1943, the last of the Mandate era. Polling date not found. (corrected from 1937-1943: Keghart lists the fourth parliament, 63 deputies, as 1937-1939.)

title: First independence-era elections, first round
why: First round 29 Aug, second round 4 Sep 1943. Independents won 36 of 55 seats; Khoury's Constitutional Bloc led to Riad Solh's government.

title: 1943 elections second round
why: Second round of the 1943 vote for the 55-seat Chamber, held six days after the first round.

title: 1947 parliamentary elections, first round
why: First round 25 May, second round 1 Jun 1947; turnout 61.45%. Historians describe the poll as heavily manipulated.

title: 1947 elections second round
why: Second round of the 55-seat Chamber vote; independents took 41 seats, Constitutional Bloc 12.

title: 1951 parliamentary elections, first round
why: First round 15 Apr, second 22 Apr 1951, for an enlarged 77-seat Chamber; turnout 54.7%. Kataeb and PSP enter.

title: 1951 elections second round
why: Second round of the 77-seat vote; independents held most seats.

title: 1953 elections held under plurality system
why: Voting ran 12 July to 9 Aug 1953 for 44 seats; first poll won on plurality, with no second round.

title: 1957 elections run 9 to 23 June
why: Disputed 66-seat vote; the page cites CIA funding for selected candidates; turnout 53.24%.

title: 1960 elections second round
why: General elections ran 12 June to 2 July 1960; independents won 68 of 99 seats.

title: 1964 parliamentary elections, first round
why: First round 5 Apr, second 3 May 1964; independents won 70 of 99 seats; Karami replaced Oweini as PM.

title: 1964 elections second round
why: Second round of the 99-seat Chamber vote; turnout 53.0%.

title: 1968 elections open, running to 7 April
why: Voting spread over 24 March to 7 April 1968; per-district dates not stated on the page.

title: 1972 elections run 16 to 30 April
why: Last vote before the civil war; 100 seats, turnout 54.38%. Existing entry dates it 9 April, this page says 16-30 April.
dup_of: Last parliamentary elections before the civil war

title: Parliament's mandate extended during civil war
why: Deputies' mandates were extended repeatedly after 1976, about 11 times by one count, until the 1992 elections. Individual dates not found. IPU states mandates were extended several times; 1976 start year not confirmed.

title: 1992 elections final phase
why: Voting ran 23 Aug to 11 Oct 1992, the first since 1972; turnout 30.35%, with a Christian boycott.

title: 1996 elections final round
why: Voting ran over successive Sundays from 18 Aug to 15 Sep 1996 (18, 25 Aug; 8, 15 Sep); turnout 43.29%.
dup_of: Parliamentary elections, Hariri list wins Beirut

title: 2000 parliamentary elections, first round
why: First round 27 Aug, second 3 Sep 2000; Hariri bloc won 26 seats; turnout 40.52%. Hariri returned as PM.

title: 2000 elections second round
why: Second round of the 128-seat vote, the first after Israel's withdrawal from the south.

title: 2005 elections open in Beirut
why: Four phases: 29 May, 5, 12 and 20 June 2005; first vote in 30 years without Syrian forces. March 14 won 69 of 128 seats.

title: 2005 elections fourth and final phase
why: North phase on 20 June closed the vote; existing entry says 19 June. Turnout about 46.5%. (corrected from 2005-06-20: EU EOM report gives North Lebanon on 19 June; Wikipedia says 20 June.)

title: Parliament passes proportional-representation electoral law
why: June 2017 law set 15 multi-member districts with confessional distribution; used first in the 2018 election. Law number not confirmed.

title: Parliament extends own term by 11 months
why: Third extension of the 2009 Parliament, passed 16 June 2017 to allow the new electoral law to be applied.

title: 2022 expatriate voting opens in Arab states
why: Lebanese in Arab countries voted 6 May; UAE and rest of world 8 May; residents voted 15 May 2022.

title: Decree 2438 sets May 2026 election dates
why: Decree 2438 set expatriate voting for 1 and 3 May and residents for 10 May 2026. The vote was later postponed.

title: Parliament postpones election, 76 votes to 41
why: Plenary vote with 4 abstentions put the May 2026 poll off two years to May 2028, citing war and displacement. Election not held.
dup_of: Parliament extends its term by two years

title: Debbas re-elected president, 42 of 44 votes
why: Chamber re-elected Charles Debbas for a second three-year term.

title: High Commissioner suspends constitution, extends Debbas term
why: Henri Ponsot suspended the constitution and extended the president's term by a year, reportedly to block a Muslim candidate.

title: Debbas resigns the presidency
why: Charles Debbas handed in his resignation; he later served as Speaker in 1934.

title: Habib Pacha Saad named president
why: Named, not elected, under the Mandate; he served to 20 Jan 1936.

title: Emile Edde takes office as president
why: Edde elected president in 1936; his term ran 20 Jan 1936 to 4 April 1941. Exact vote date and count not found.

title: Edde's first presidential term ends
why: Edde served until April 1941; Alfred Naccache succeeded him under French appointment.

title: Khoury elected president: 44 votes in first round
why: 47 deputies attended; Bechara el-Khoury won on the first round. Source gives these counts.
dup_of: Bechara el-Khoury elected first independent president

title: French arrest leaders; Edde named president briefly
why: Emile Edde held the post 11 to 22 Nov 1943 under French appointment; independence leaders were freed on 22 Nov.

title: Constitutional law of 22 May 1948
why: Listed among the amendments in the consolidated constitution text; the text does not state its content here.

title: Chamoun elected president, 74 of 76 votes
why: First round win. Existing entry gives the date; this adds the count.

title: Chehab wins second ballot, 48 votes
why: First ballot 43 for Chehab, 10 for Eddé; second ballot 48 to 7. 56 of 66 deputies voted; PM Solh abstained.

title: Helou elected president, 92 of 99 votes
why: First-round win over Pierre Gemayel, who got 5.

title: Frangieh wins third vote 50 to 49; second invalidated
why: First round Sarkis 45, Frangieh 38; second round voided over an extra ballot; Frangieh won the third by one vote.
dup_of: Suleiman Frangieh elected president by one vote

title: Sarkis elected in second round, 66 votes
why: First round 63, second round 66; only 69 of 99 deputies attended amid fighting. Taking office on 23 Sep 1976.

title: Hrawi elected at Chtaura, 47 of 52 deputies
why: Vote held at Chtaura after Moawad's death; Aoun refused to recognise it. Sources differ between 46 and 47 votes.

title: Parliament extends Hrawi's term by three years
why: Constitutional amendment passed by two-thirds majority; date comes from a search summary of Hrawi's page.
dup_of: Hrawi's term extended by three years

title: Lahoud elected with all 118 votes present
why: First round, one ballot, 118 votes. Contemporary WRMEA report gives 15 Oct; Wikipedia's election page says 13 Oct. Article 49 amended once for an army commander.
dup_of: Army chief Emile Lahoud elected president

title: Constitutional Law 585 extends Lahoud's term
why: Law of 4 Sep 2004 is the latest amendment in the consolidated constitution; it extended the president's term by three years. Parliament voted 3 Sep 2004 (96 of 128); law number 585 and 4 Sep date from a WIPO Lex summary, not independently fetched.

title: Suleiman elected with 118 of 127 votes, ending vacuum
why: Vacuum began 24 Nov 2007 after about 19 postponed sessions; the Doha Agreement of 21 May 2008 enabled the vote.

title: Aoun elected on 46th session, 83 of 127 votes
why: Presidential vacuum of 25 May 2014 to 31 Oct 2016 ends; 45 earlier sessions had failed. Won in the fourth round.

title: Joseph Aoun elected on 13th attempt, 99 of 128 votes
why: Won in the second round; parliament had failed 12 times since Oct 2022. Vacuum of about 26 months ends.

title: Constitutional law of 17 October 1927
why: Amends the 1926 constitution; the amendment abolished the Senate and made the legislature a single chamber.

title: Constitutional law of 8 May 1929
why: Amendment to articles on legislative procedure, listed in the consolidated constitution text.

title: March 1943 amendment ends appointed deputies
why: Decree by the French High Commissioner abolished appointed deputies; all members of the Chamber must be elected. (corrected from 1943-03: Decree/Order 129 of 18 March 1943.)

title: Constitutional law of 9 November 1943
why: Listed amendment of the independence crisis; the existing entry dates the abolition of Mandate provisions 8 Nov.

title: Constitutional law of 21 January 1947
why: Amended various articles of the constitution, per the consolidated text.

title: January 1976 amendment lets presidential vote be held early
why: Allowed Sarkis to be elected months before Frangieh's term ended in September 1976; exact date not found.

title: Municipal elections held in 1952
why: Municipal elections held in 1952/53 per the Arab Reform Initiative; the next ones came in 1963. (corrected from 1952/53: MERIP and LCPS give 1952 only.)

title: Municipal elections resume after 35 years
why: Held on successive Sundays from 24 May to 14 June 1998; first since 1963. Dates come from a search summary.

title: Municipal elections held in the South
why: South Lebanon voted after the 2000 Israeli withdrawal; date not given in the source.

title: Municipal elections held, May 2004
why: Second post-war municipal cycle; exact phase dates not confirmed.

title: 2010 municipal elections begin, four phases
why: Phases on 2, 9, 23 and 30 May: Mount Lebanon and Beirut, Bekaa, South, then North.

title: 2016 municipal elections begin in Beirut and Bekaa
why: Voting 8, 15, 22 and 29 May. Beirut Madinati won 30.2% but no seats; existing entry says about 40%.
dup_of: Beirut Madinati takes about 32% of the vote in Beirut municipal election

title: Municipal elections postponed first time
why: Due in May 2022; deferred over logistics and overlap with parliamentary elections.

title: Parliament extends municipal councils to May 2024
why: Second postponement, citing lack of funds; new deadline 31 May 2024.

title: Parliament extends municipal councils to May 2025
why: Third postponement, citing the war in the south; 31 May 2025 became the final legal date.

title: Municipal elections: North Lebanon and Akkar vote
why: Second weekend of the 2025 municipal cycle after nine years.

title: Municipal elections: Beirut, Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel vote
why: Beirut Unites Us won 23 of 24 seats; Hezbollah-Amal won all 80 contested Baalbek-Hermel municipalities.

title: Municipal elections: South and Nabatieh vote
why: Final phase, moved to Saturday 24 May around Resistance and Liberation Day; overall turnout 39%.

title: UNSC Resolution 427 raises UNIFIL to 6,000
why: Vote 12-0-2; approved the increase from 4,000 and urged Israel to complete withdrawal.

title: UNSC Resolution 501 raises UNIFIL ceiling by 1,000
why: Increased the UNIFIL troop ceiling by 1,000, as the Force Commander recommended and Lebanon supported.

title: UNSC Resolution 511 extends UNIFIL, adds interim tasks
why: Extended the mandate two months to 19 Aug 1982 and authorised supplementary interim tasks; 13-0-2.

title: UNSC Resolution 518 demands end to Beirut restrictions
why: Unanimous demand that Israel and all parties observe Council resolutions and lift restrictions on Beirut for humanitarian aid.

title: UNSC Resolution 1697 extends UNIFIL one month
why: Unanimous; short extension to 31 Aug 2006 to let the Council weigh future arrangements while war continued.

title: UNSC Resolution 1748 extends Hariri commission

title: UNSC Resolution 1815 extends Hariri commission
why: Unanimous; extended UNIIIC mandate to 31 Dec 2008.

title: UNSC Resolution 1852 extends UNIIIC to February 2009

title: Friends of Lebanon conference
why: Convened with Secretary of State Christopher and PM Hariri; 29 countries and seven institutions took part. Details from a search summary.

title: Paris I: first donor meeting on Lebanon's economy
why: Hosted by France with World Bank, EIB and EC; raised about 500 million euros, per a search summary.

title: Rome II ministerial meeting backs Lebanese security forces
why: Rome ministerial of the International Support Group for Lebanon, backing the army and internal security; about 40 delegations.

title: Paris conference for Lebanon's people and sovereignty: $1bn pledged
why: About 70 states and organisations; $800m humanitarian and $200m for Lebanon's security forces, per press reports.
